Worksheet 1 | SL Core

School Library

Use this first. The database is deliberately simple so students can read the schema, identify keys and relationships, and practise SELECT, FROM, WHERE, AND, and OR before moving on to sorting, pattern matching, joins, or grouped reports.

SELECT FROM WHERE AND OR
Open SQL Playground All SQL worksheets

Dataset

  • 3 tables: STUDENT, BOOK, LOAN
  • Two one-to-many relationships through foreign keys
  • Clean enough for first schema and integrity questions

Syllabus Links

  • A3.1.1 relational features, benefits, and limitations
  • A3.2.1 conceptual, logical, and physical schema
  • A3.3.2 core retrieval with filtering conditions

Before You Start

  • Open the table list and schema view before Section 1.
  • Stay with single-table queries on this worksheet.
  • Do not worry about joins yet. That comes next.
1

Read the Database

Start by reading the structure, not by writing queries.

  1. A3.1.1 Primary keys

    Name the three tables and identify the primary key in each one.

  2. A3.1.1 Foreign keys

    Which table stores the foreign keys back to STUDENT and BOOK, and what do those links represent in the real world?

  3. A3.2.1 Schema levels

    State which schema level would show the ERD, which would show the field names and data types, and which would show storage or indexing choices.

  4. A3.1.1 Evaluation

    Give one benefit and one limitation of storing this library system in a relational database rather than across separate spreadsheets.

2

Retrieve the Right Columns

Build the habit of selecting only the table and columns you need.

Reference pattern — SELECT and FROM 
-- Every column from one table
SELECT *
FROM table_name;

-- Only the columns you need
SELECT column_a, column_b
FROM table_name;

-- Rename a column in the result set
SELECT column_a AS useful_label
FROM table_name;

SELECT chooses the columns to return. FROM chooses the table those columns come from.

  1. A3.3.2 SELECT *

    Display every row and column from STUDENT.

  2. A3.3.2 Specific columns

    Show only Title and Author from BOOK.

  3. A3.3.2 Chosen fields

    Return StudentID, FirstName, and LastName for every student.

  4. A3.3.2 Book details

    Show Title, Genre, and PublishedYear from BOOK.

3

Filter Rows

Now narrow the result set using conditions.

Reference pattern — WHERE, AND, OR 
-- Match one value exactly
SELECT *
FROM table_name
WHERE status_column = 'Open';

-- AND means both conditions must be true
SELECT *
FROM table_name
WHERE group_column = 'A'
  AND score_column >= 80;

-- OR means either condition can be true
SELECT *
FROM table_name
WHERE type_column = 'Science'
   OR type_column = 'Technology';

WHERE filters rows. AND makes the query stricter; OR widens it to allow either condition.

  1. A3.3.2 WHERE

    Show the first name, last name, and tutor group for students in 12B.

  2. A3.3.2 OR

    List the titles and genres of books where the genre is Science or Technology.

  3. A3.3.2 WHERE

    Find every loan row where ReturnStatus is Overdue.

  4. A3.3.2 AND

    Return the loan record for student 1003 where the book is still On Loan.

  5. A3.1.1 Integrity

    Explain why a new loan row with StudentID = 9999 should be rejected when referential integrity is enforced.

Model Answers — School Library

Section 1

1
Keys and structure STUDENT(StudentID), BOOK(BookID), and LOAN(LoanID). LOAN.StudentID and LOAN.BookID are foreign keys.
2
Schema levels ERD = conceptual schema. Field names, data types, and keys = logical schema. Storage and indexing = physical schema.

Section 2

3
Example retrieval 
SELECT *
FROM STUDENT;

SELECT Title, Author
FROM BOOK;

Section 3

4
Filtering examples 
SELECT FirstName, LastName, TutorGroup
FROM STUDENT
WHERE TutorGroup = '12B';

SELECT Title, Genre
FROM BOOK
WHERE Genre = 'Science' OR Genre = 'Technology';

SELECT *
FROM LOAN
WHERE StudentID = 1003
  AND ReturnStatus = 'On Loan';
5
Referential integrity The foreign key in LOAN must match an existing primary key in STUDENT. If student 9999 does not exist, the row would create an orphan record and should be rejected.
